Teeth with incomplete root formation:
â¢ Allow eruption without intervention
â¢ If no movement within few weeks, initiate orthodontic repositioning.
â¢ If tooth is intruded more than 7mm, reposition surgically or orthodontically.

â¢ Allow eruption without intervention if tooth intruded less than 3mm. If no movement after 2-4 weeks, reposition surgically or orthodontically before ankylosis can develop.

IAPD Bangkok Declaration:

â¢ The purpose of this Declaration is to gain worldwide support for an evidence-based definition and a common understanding of the evidence around the aetiology, risk factors, and interventions to reduce Early Childhood Caries (ECC), as well as to mobilize collaborative approaches and policies to diminish this chronic disease.

â¢ Early Childhood Caries (ECC) is defined as the presence of one or more decayed (non-cavitated or cavitated lesions), missing or filled (due to caries) surfaces, in any primary tooth of a child under six years of age.
â¢ To reduce the prevalence and burden of ECC worldwide, the IAPD Bangkok Declaration recommends the following actions: Four key areas requiring action with multiple stakeholders are as follows:
- Raise awareness of ECC with parents/caregivers, dentists, dental hygienists, physicians, nurses, health professionals, and other stakeholders.
- Limit sugar intake in foods and drinks and avoid free sugars for children under 2 years of age.
- Perform twice daily tooth brushing with fluoridated tooth-paste (at least 1000 ppm) in all children, using an age-appropriate amount of paste.

- Provide preventive guidance within the first year of life by a health professional or community health worker (building on existing programsâeg vaccinationsâwhere possible) and ideally, referral to a dentist for comprehensive continuing care.",

RECENT PAPERS 2020-21 PEDODONTICS,6,"A mother came to the clinic with 8 years old child and complained of very large front teeth, her elder son of 12 years also has similar problem, on clinical examination child has short upper lip, everted lower lip, deep mentolabial sulcus with a distal step molar relation; however no oral habits could be elicited from the patient, what is the treatment?",Wait and watch,Activator,Herbst appliance,bionator,B,"B' [Check Explanation Below]

Deep mentolabial sulcus is usually found in retropositioned mandible. According to longitudinal study by Bishara et al, cases with a distal step occlusion in the primary dentition resulted in a class II permanent first molar malocclusion, which will not self-correct with growth. A distal step molar relation will lock the mandible and give distal unfavorable component of force with little probability of turning into Class-I. Giving activator (also known as eruption guidance appliance) can guide the rest of the occlusion and at the same time allowing mandible to grow. Activator is indicated in growing young children for the correction of class II malocclusion, which is mainly due to smaller mandible.
If the question was with end-on-molar relation, then we can go with wait and watch (Option B) as growth spurt will lead on to class 1 relation.",

Treatment Consideration in children with intellectual disability: The dentist must first assess the child's mental level so as to gauge the level of cooperation to be expected and make adjustments accordingly:
â¢ Short attention span, restlessness, hyperactivity and erratic emotional behavior characterize MR patients undergoing dental treatment.
â¢ Familiarize the patient to the office and dental personnel to reduce his/her fear of the unknown before undertaking any treatment.
â¢ Speech must be slow and simple.
â¢ Only one instruction at a time should be given.
â¢ Children should be managed with a blend of kindness and firmness.
â¢ TSD (Tell Show Do) and TLC (Tender Loving Care) approach in mild cases, whereas sedation in moderate cases.
â¢ General anaesthesia may be indicated in cases where adequate levels of co-operation can not be achieved or where extensive rehabilitation is required.
â¢ Carefully listen to the patient as these children often have trouble with communication.
â¢ Appointments should be short and scheduled during the early part of the day.",

â¢ A splint has been defined as 'an apparatus used to support, protect or immobilize teeth that have been loosened, replanted, fractured or subjected to certain endodontic surgical procedures'.
â¢ Splinting has been advocated after repositioning and stabilization of a tooth/ a group of teeth and to optimize healing outcomes for the pulp and/or the periodontal ligament.
Splint Types:
Composite and wire splints: flexible splints and the wire has a diameter of no greater than 0.3â 0.4 mm.
Composite and fishing line splints: An alternative where fishing line replaces wire and the line is secured with composite resin.
Fibre splints: use a polyethylene or Kevlar fibre mesh and are attached either with an unfilled resin and/or with composite resin.
The titanium trauma splint (TTS): is a flexible splint made of titanium, 0.2 mm thick and 2.8 mm wide.
Orthondontic wire and bracket splints: involves orthodontic brackets bonded to the teeth with a resin-based orthodontic cement and connected with a light 0.014 NiTi flexible wire.
Arch bar splints: A metal bar is bent into the shape of the arch and fixed with ligature wires.
Wire ligature splints: are sometimes used by oral surgeons in clinics where dental splinting materials may not be available.
A splint for medical emergency departments: Stomahesive (ConvaTec Inc.), a skin barrier adhesive material used for superficial skin trauma.",

â¢ Glutaraldehyde produces rapid surface fixation. Narrow zone of eosinophillic stained and compressed fixed tissue is found beneath the area of application which blends with underlying normal pulp. It was noted that increasing the concentration and longer time improves fixation and suggested the use of 4% Glutaraldehyde for 4 minutes or 8% Glutaraldehyde for 2 minutes.
â¢ Sandra Maria et al. suggested the use of 2% for 5 minutes. Presently, 2% glutaraldehyde for 5 minutes is used for pulpotomy.

The act of eating or drinking can be broken down into four main phases:
â¢ Oral phase (i.e. suckling or mastication, and the transportation of the bolus towards the pharynx)
â¢ Triggering of the swallowing reflex
â¢ Pharyngeal phase (i.e. transportation of the bolus through the pharynx), and

Introduced by Joseph Wolpe, Systematic desensitization is traditionally used with a child patient with existing anxiety in the dental situation and to eliminate a dental phobia. It has two important elements:

This technique has been used for patients with psychiatric problems regarding some fears. The therapist creates a list of steps arranged as a hierarchy from the least to the most stressful:
â¢ The patient, while in a state of deep relaxation, is exposed one step at a time. Each step is presented repeatedly until there is no evidence of stress or antagonism on the patient's part.

â¢ On satisfactory completion of the hierarchy procedure, the patient is desensitized to the predominant fear. In a dental situation, the procedures needed for the child from the initial appointment to the final appointment are arranged from the least painful/fearful ones to the most (e.g., procedures needing local anesthesia such as pulp therapy and extractions).
